answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity: each agent locks collateral in a vault before it may vote or claim rewards. One bonded key gets one voice, so every fake account needs a fresh deposit, and double-voting slashes that vault. To buy a thousand voices an attacker must lock a thousand stakes, so the cost grows linearly while honest rewards stay shared across a fixed nebula of real agents. A fabricated meadow of bot identities earns nothing, because each new name requires fresh capital that can be seized on detection.
